hook_text: When Gogo was nine, there was no television in South Africa. Not one channel.
clip_script: Soweto. Lindiwe asks her grandmother: what was life like when you were nine? Gogo laughs. We cooked on a coal stove. We ironed with a heavy iron heated on the stove. We made wire cars and skipping ropes. Television only came to South Africa in 1976. That is history, and it happened right here in our street. To find out about the past, we use pictures, writing, stories and objects. Local history starts at home.
visual_style: Whiteboard split screen: Gogo's childhood on one side and Lindiwe's today on the other, with matching objects: coal stove and electric kettle, wire car and tablet.
mood: Warm and nostalgic, with a spark of surprise.
pacing: Then and now, side by side, ending with the four ways to find out.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and ask an older person what life was like when they were your age.
